sections.text_helper: Section 31.3.22 "Output idle state override" in chapter 31 (Advanced-control timers (TIM1/TIM8)), RM0522 Rev 1, page 1017.
sections.section_content:
It is possible to override the outputs states when they are disabled (ie MOE bit reset in
TIM_BDTR). This feature can be used to apply specific patterns prior to start PWM
operations, for instance to refresh bootstrap capacitors of power switch gate drivers.
The OOC control bit in the TIM_OOR register acts as following:
• OOC= 0: 0: tim_ocx and tim_ocxn outputs are in the default idle state
• OOC=1: tim_ocx and tim_ocxn outputs are forced in an idle state defined with
OOSx/OOSxN bits in the TIM_OOR register
The OOC bit can only be modified when the outputs are in idle state (MOE = 0). It is cleared
by hardware when the MOE bit is set, and the deadtime generator ensures there’s no
deadtime violation on complementary outputs.
The OOSx/OOSxN bits in the TIM_OOR register cannot be modified as long as LOCK level
1, 2 or 3 has been programmed (LOCK bits in TIM_BDTR register).
